intro: When you search for criminal lawyers near me, you likely need someone who can advise and represent you at the police station or in court, often at short notice. Criminal solicitors deal with everything from police interviews to magistrates' and Crown Court hearings. We introduce you to a suitable UK professional who can quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for criminal lawyers near me usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for criminal lawyers near me need urgent, local help with a police investigation or court case.
needs: You have been arrested or asked to attend a police interview and need advice before speaking to the police.
You have been charged with an offence and need representation at a magistrates' court hearing.
Your case has been sent to the Crown Court and you need a solicitor to prepare your defence.
You are under investigation for an alleged offence and want advice on your rights and options.
You need to know whether you qualify for legal aid for your court case.
context_heading: Understanding your right to legal advice
context: If you are arrested or asked to attend a police interview, you have the right to free legal advice at the police station. It is important not to discuss the case with the police before you have received that advice.
For court proceedings, legal aid may be available depending on your circumstances and the type of case. You can ask the solicitor you speak to whether you are likely to qualify.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Explain whether you have been arrested, asked to attend a police interview, charged with an offence, or are due to appear in court.
Say which police station or court is involved, if you know.
Give the date and time of any interview, hearing or deadline you are facing.
Describe the nature of the alleged offence in brief, without going into detail you are unsure about.
Mention whether you have already spoken to the police or another solicitor.
State whether you are asking about legal aid or will be paying privately.
questions: Are you regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority or the relevant body for my part of the UK?
Will you be the person handling my case, and if not, who will?
Can you represent me at the police station for free?
Do you think I might qualify for legal aid for my court case?
What information do you need from me before the police interview or court hearing?
How will you keep me informed about what is happening with my case?

faqs.q: Do I have to pay for a solicitor at the police station?
faqs.a: No, you have the right to free legal advice at the police station. This applies whether you are arrested or attending voluntarily for an interview.

faqs.q: Can I get legal aid for my criminal case?
faqs.a: Legal aid may be available for court cases, depending on your financial circumstances and the type of case. You should ask the solicitor you speak to whether you are likely to qualify.

faqs.q: What should I do if the police want to interview me?
faqs.a: You should not discuss the case with the police before receiving legal advice. Ask for a solicitor and tell iComply so we can introduce you to a criminal solicitor near you.

faqs.q: How do I check that someone is a qualified solicitor?
faqs.a: The word "lawyer" is not protected, so check that the person is a solicitor, chartered legal executive or another authorised professional. You can check a solicitor's details on the Solicitors Regulation Authority's register for England and Wales, or the Law Society of Scotland or Law Society of Northern Ireland for those jurisdictions.

extra: When you search for criminal lawyers near me, you are likely weighing up several local firms and want to know how to choose between them. Criminal work is often urgent, so it helps to focus on who can see you quickly and who regularly handles cases like yours at your local police station or court. Ask each firm whether they offer a free initial consultation and how they would handle your first steps.

It is also worth checking that the person you speak to is actually a solicitor or another authorised professional, because the word "lawyer" is not protected. You can look up a solicitor on the Solicitors Regulation Authority's register for England and Wales, or the Law Society of Scotland or Law Society of Northern Ireland if you are elsewhere in the UK. This tells you they are regulated and must carry professional indemnity insurance.

Cost is another factor, but criminal cases can be funded in different ways: free advice at the police station, legal aid for court if you qualify, or private payment. Ask each firm to explain which applies to you and what you would be expected to pay. A short conversation with a few local solicitors can help you compare how confident and clear they are about your situation.

extra_faqs.q: How do I compare criminal solicitors near me if I don't know any?
extra_faqs.a: Start by making a short list of local firms that handle criminal cases. Check that the person you would see is a solicitor or authorised professional on the relevant register, and ask about their experience with cases like yours, their availability and their approach to fees. A brief phone call to each can give you a sense of how they communicate.

extra_faqs.q: Can I change solicitors if I'm not happy with the one I have?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, you can usually change solicitors, but it is worth understanding any implications for your case and any costs incurred so far. Speak to your current solicitor first if possible, and ask the new firm how they would handle the transfer. If you are receiving legal aid, the new firm will need to check that you still qualify.
